solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Annual ceremony convened with wizard's backing

indicators.note: backing means the two pieces are read from the end to the start

parts.note: a body that convened sat, as a court or committee sits
wizard and fab are both dated slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A yearly awards night meets with the support of a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SATFAB around. 'Wizard' is old British slang for marvellous, like fab.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Academy film awards are handed out at a yearly televised gala.

clue.text: Go after second rate reading matter, attacking furiously

indicators.note: after places the word for go behind the other pieces

parts.note: B is second class, second rate
lit is short for literature
go and zing both mean energy, vigour

explanation.surface: Someone tears into poor-quality books, savaging them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' here is a noun meaning pep, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Blitzing is mounting a sudden, intense assault, as in a wartime air raid.

clue.text: Note Cockney's kindness being spoken of

indicators.note: being spoken of says the word is to be heard as pronounced

parts.note: a favour is a kindness; in a Cockney accent the word comes out with an 'eye' vowel

explanation.surface: A Londoner's good turn is noted by others.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which turns the 'ay' sound into 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pound banknote is called this in informal British speech.

clue.text: Bearing the strain

definitions.meaning: a strain is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Putting up with the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person's manner; the other is a melody, both covered by this short word.

clue.text: Complaint coming up that must be got around?

definitions.meaning: decompression sickness, which strikes divers who rise to the surface too fast
curves in a road, which a driver has to steer round

explanation.surface: An objection is raised that will need a workaround.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' means an illness here, and 'coming up' is a diver ascending.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers' sickness and road curves share this name.

clue.text: Is owner of bank considered? Not so

parts.note: someone who is owner of a thing has it
a bank of seats is a tier, one row above another

explanation.surface: A question whether a bank's proprietor is well thought of, answered in the negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, but it is a row or level.
explanation.definitionFit: Less considered means more rushed, the comparative of hasty.

clue.text: Trumpet-blowing of dance music dwarf covered in life story

indicators.note: covered in places the music and dwarf inside the life story

parts.note: bio is short for biography
ragga is a Jamaican dance music style
Doc is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs

explanation.surface: Boasting found in a biography about dance tunes and a little man.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing one's own trumpet is boasting, and this word means empty boastfulness.

clue.text: Run in with box for tool

parts.note: to run in a criminal is to arrest them, to nail them
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: A fight-related scrap involving a box, swapped for an implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run in' is slang for arrest, not a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: This implement drives nail heads below a wooden surface; it is a carpenter's hand device.

clue.text: Those in favour tipped 17 for promotion, maybe

indicators.note: tipped means upended, so in this down entry the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: pets are favourites, as a teacher's pet
17 across is riding; a jockey riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: Favoured people backed a cross-reference for advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing a jockey is 'up' on a horse, meaning riding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in rank or level is an example of advancement, so it fits with 'maybe'.

clue.text: What a welcome for Mary after start of birthday function

indicators.note: after puts the remaining pieces behind that opening letter
start of picks the opening letter of birthday

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
Ave, the angel's greeting in the Hail Mary

explanation.surface: A greeting for Mary is offered at a birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' looks like a party noun but is the verb meaning to work properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that behaves works correctly, so the verb serves as a synonym for operating.

clue.text: Ted escapes being turned over, maybe, in Scottish town

indicators.note: escapes means the name Ted gets out of the longer word

parts.note: the state of being upside down is invertedness

explanation.surface: Ted flees a possible capsizing near a Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the chief town of the Highlands, at the mouth of the River Ness.

clue.text: Gangster and president with much in common

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A mobster and a head of state turn out to be similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are similar have many shared features.

clue.text: Lightly touching on love for farming method

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the touching word after the word for love

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring
grazing is brushing lightly against

explanation.surface: A gentle caress on a lover is presented as an agricultural practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock are fed cut grass brought indoors rather than left to roam pastures: an agricultural system.

clue.text: Really fancy package, round, wrapped by West Indian

indicators.note: wrapped by places the package and round inside the Indian

parts.note: a Goan comes from Goa, on India's west coast
a bundle is a package
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A parcel and a round of drinks are bundled up by a Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' wants to be Caribbean; it is a Goan.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom means to be very keen on or enthusiastic about something.

clue.text: Means to improve reputation with posh girl

parts.note: PR, public relations, polishes an image
U means upper class

explanation.surface: A well-to-do young woman hires spin doctors to burnish her image.
explanation.definitionFit: A short female first name, from Prudence.

clue.text: Artistic movement of green and white horse?

parts.note: green means inexperienced or new
white horses are foam-topped waves

explanation.surface: An art school whose emblem is a green and white horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white horse' is a crested wave, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A label for the French film movement and later pop music trend.

clue.text: No ducking the consequences of its successful negotiation?

definitions.text: No ducking the consequences of its successful negotiation?

parts.words: No ducking the consequences of its successful negotiation?
parts.note: a horse clearing this obstacle avoids landing in the pool, so no soaking follows

explanation.surface: A deal well struck means nobody can dodge its results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiation' means getting over an obstacle, and 'ducking' a soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase fence with a pool behind it, which horses fall into if they fail.

clue.text: A division of history of equestrian art?

definitions.meaning: one of Yorkshire's three historical administrative parts
the skill of travelling on horseback

explanation.surface: A section of a history of horsemanship.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was long split into three of these parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old county subdivision and horsemanship.

clue.text: After filming, maybe, run to take on champion

parts.note: to take on an opponent is to play them
to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A runner decides to challenge the title holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Once something is recorded, the replay of the footage is this kind of run.

clue.text: Plays in ways not conforming to expectation?

indicators.note: in places the odd word inside the ways

parts.note: St is street, so two make streets, ways
rum means odd, strange

explanation.surface: Someone plays in unconventional styles.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucking a guitar's strings is a way of performing on it.

clue.text: Declined to hug as filthy

indicators.note: to hug means the word for declined wraps around the other

parts.note: slid means fell, declined
qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Someone refused an embrace because they were dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declined' looks like refused but means fell.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid describes extremely dirty and unpleasant surroundings.

clue.text: Local brewing house opens to provide it?

definitions.text: Local brewing house opens to provide it?

indicators.note: opens means the house abbreviation goes inside the mix
brewing stirs the letters of local into a new mix

explanation.surface: A pub's brewery opening up to supply drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram made by 'brewing' is ALCOL. A 'local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, so the whole clue pictures where the drink comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub and its brewery exist to supply intoxicating drink.

clue.text: Answer kid's composed

parts.note: to kid is to tease; the 's is just is, a link

explanation.surface: The response a child has written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and calm, as soldiers standing easy.

clue.text: Mountaineering aid seen in distance, above fell

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the coldness word on top

parts.note: ice is coldness or aloofness, emotional distance
to fell a tree is to axe it

explanation.surface: Climbing gear spotted far off, on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a Lake District hill but is the verb to cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers use this pick to cut steps and arrest falls on frozen slopes.

clue.text: Return of legendary winger's brother

indicators.note: return of means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird

explanation.surface: A mythical footballer's sibling comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests football but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of surprise, as in 'Oh brother!'

clue.text: Fresher you mentored in biblical work

indicators.note: fresher hints at newly shaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A first-year student you tutored in Bible studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresher' is a British term for a first-year university student.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Large feline in spring, heading off

indicators.note: heading off takes away the first letter

parts.note: to pounce is to spring

explanation.surface: A big cat leaps, then sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Gets gunboat back defying odds in exploit

indicators.note: back reads the picked letters in reverse
defying odds keeps only the even letters

explanation.surface: Someone gets a gunboat back against all odds in a daring feat.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters ESUBA are turned around by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to take unfair advantage of them, mistreat them.

clue.text: Old province of Asia, until dissolved

indicators.note: dissolved breaks the letters up and lets them re-form

explanation.surface: A former territory of Asia lasted until it was broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Asia' misleads: it was a Roman province in Iberia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusitania was the Roman region roughly matching modern Portugal.

clue.text: Tango without what it takes?

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance lacking the essentials.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'it takes two to tango'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying says this many are needed to dance the tango, a pair.

clue.text: Turnover from enterprise initially millions a year — then nothing

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of enterprise

parts.note: M is millions
p.a. is per annum, a year
nada is Spanish for nothing

explanation.surface: A business's revenue went from millions a year to zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like business revenue but is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a folded filled pastry, and an empanada is a Latin American one.

clue.text: Put out by kiss that's tender but worth very little

parts.note: KO is a knockout, putting a boxer out
a peck is a light kiss

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a kiss that's affectionate but meaningless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' means legal tender, money, not affectionate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian coin worth one hundredth of a rouble, so it is money of tiny value.
